chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: Dancers, singers and the backers of the show
summary: The show added dancers and singers including the Durmettes, with backing from a wealthy family, and he bought the Dominoes' station wagon.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: : Well, of course, by this time --
Had dancers. Had this Sonya Millburn dancer from Canada who was supposed have been so good and I had --
(Inaudible) supposed to be?
What was her name? The girl was with Bullmoose Jackson. She had a good record out.
Not Anestine Allen.

No, some other girl. And then I had another girl called -- the girl that looked just like Lena Horne. She was with Muhamma (inaudible), pretty girl, and she was doing a location over there in Jersey. We got her costume and she was doing the rumba rhythm stuff. I had another girl who sung ballads, __________. __________ recorded all that.
Oh, he did?
And made up a lot of stock cards. I had backing, though. I had -- Quentin Jackson's mother was backing, you know.
She was backing you?
Yeah, (inaudible).
Well, did Quentin Jackson's mother have money?
Quentin Jackson is one of the lawyers in New York, big family, yeah.
Oh, you don't mean Quentin Jackson, the
No, no. This guy -- these people are in big real estate.
Oh.
These money people.
Yeah.

So, I didn't have to use too much money because I already owned a big Cadillac. I bought the nine-passenger station wagon from the Dominoes. They got a hit record on Stardust or something and they had just bought a Desoto and I got it from them for about $2,000 or something -- two or $3,000, because they all decided they wanted two Cadillacs and that was a brand new car.
(Laughter.)
And so we had plenty of transportation. Had about four cars on the tour. But had ________ show. We played (unintelligible).
